## Session 2026-11-16 — L20: downloads, the first run and Apple Intelligence say what is happening: the size the series takes on the device, measured, Cancel All, a failed download shown with Retry, and why a summary cannot be made (#1920)

**What and why.** Row L20 of the plan of record from 2026-11-15, started by the plan's session once #1943 had merged (`914ccac8`). From `v2` at `914ccac8`, on `claude/l20-downloads-first-run-1eedf4`. Four of the UI and UX review's findings (HCD-1, HCD-2, HCD-3, HCD-5), filed as #1920, whose body was the brief with the plan's L20 bullet and the review's §3 row L20: one pull request, a commit for each finding and a docs commit. App and test code on both platforms; no `FRUSCoreKit/` change, no index version, no CloudKit change (a failed download is kept in memory, never on a `@Model`). The issue's line numbers were at `4a269a35`; each was read again on this tree (`CollectionEntryInspector.swift`'s Regenerate had moved from 1163 to 1178).

**Asked of the owner before any edit, HCD-1's figure.** The plan and the issue had the caption gain *about 13 GB once indexed*, from the storage hub's *9–10 GB of index* and the Quick Start's *roughly 13 GB*. The brief asked for the total to be checked against a measured full index if one was kept. Two were: full 553-volume libraries at index version 74 from the retake sittings, an iPad Pro 13-inch simulator's (`~/Library/Caches/FRUS-Explorer/t1/pre-t1/…`) and the Mac check copy's home (`…/q1/mac/home`). Each held 3,339,186,418 bytes of volume XML, 140,994,857 of figure images, 162,423,117 of match files and an index of 3,571,359,744 (iPad) or 3,577,819,136 (Mac) bytes, of which 170,347 and 171,330 pages of 4 KB were free, left by the re-index to version 74 until Compact Database; an index as first built (version 71, kept from 2026-10-21) was 2,883,416,064 bytes with 2,490 pages free. So the series takes 6.5 to 7.2 GB on a device once indexed, and the hub's figures dated from a measurement of 2026-05-31 (a 10.09 GB index on the Mac, 8.77 GB on iOS), when the index was three times its present size; why it shrank was not traced. The whole iPad container was 7.58 GB with the optional 310 MB query encoder. The owner chose **"7 GB, hub too (Recommended)"**: the caption says about 7 GB, and the hub's sentences, its estimate and the docs are brought to the measurement in the same row.

**Changed.**
- **HCD-1, the first download's size on the device** (`bca443d6`). The caption reads *553+ volumes · ≈ 3.5 GB to download, about 7 GB once indexed — the entire series, fully offline. Recommended for full functionality.* under its key, `onboarding.scope.caption.corpus.v2 %lld`, the owner's default and *Recommended* kept (C1, 2026-09-30). `StorageReport.indexOverheadFactor`, which sizes Free Up Space's rows, is 0.86, the index in use against the XML, where it was 2.8; apportioned by each volume's share of the stored text it runs from 0.71 to 1.01 per volume (5th to 95th percentile). Both hubs' Storage & Index footer (*roughly 3.3 GB of XML plus 3 to 3.5 GB of search index*), Entire Corpus line (*plus about as much again in search index*) and Free Up Space note give the measurement; the copy scan's settled text for `settings.hub.browse.corpus.detail` is brought to it, with the reason beside it. `CorpusScaleLiteralsTests` requires both sizes in the caption.
- **HCD-2, Cancel All** (`616ea966`). `DownloadManager.cancelAll()` cancels every download, running, waiting in the queue or waiting out a failed attempt's backoff, reports each volume cancelled once (so Keeping Current and the indexing queue let go of it), empties the saved queue, and in production cancels every transfer the background session holds, an earlier process's among them (`BackgroundDownloadEngine.cancelAllDownloads()`); nothing on disk is touched. **Found on the way:** a cancel during a retry's backoff did not hold. The volume was neither running nor queued then, so the cancel reported nothing, and the scheduled retry put it back in the queue. The retry now runs only while the volume's address is still held, which both cancels drop. Callers: `ResetService.resetLocalData`, first, before it deletes a file, so Reset This Device and Erase Everything, whose saved queue used to resume at the next launch online; onboarding's Back from Ready (`backFromReady()`); and **Cancel All**, above iOS's Active Downloads rows when more than one volume is queued, and on a new queue line under the Mac hub's buttons (*553 volumes in the download queue*), each asking first (*Stop downloading 553 volumes?*, *Cancel All Downloads* or *Keep Downloading*), its question hung on the button. Back from Ready stops every download, as the plan and the issue have it, a queue kept from before onboarding included: Fix iCloud Sync is the one way into onboarding that keeps one. The Mac's full Active Downloads list stays for after 1.0.
- **HCD-3, a failed download shown with Retry** (`96727cf6`). `AppState.downloadFailures` keeps each volume's last `DownloadFailure`, in memory, from the download manager's `onTransferFinished` (`recordDownloadOutcome`); a volume that lands, or enters the queue again by any path, forgets it. `DownloadFailureNotice` shows the failure in Keeping Current's words (`KeepingCurrentCopy.failure`) with **Retry** in Download Volume's place, on the iPhone and iPad volume page and in the Mac's Corpus Browser, whose page used to stay on *Downloading…* for good and now returns to its prompt; each page posts the line at high priority as the failure arrives. The queue-wide wording stays for after 1.0.
- **HCD-5, why a summary cannot be made** (`534d0516`). `AppleIntelligenceAvailability` (`AppleIntelligenceProvider.swift`) reads `SystemLanguageModel.default.availability` as available, switched off, model not ready or not eligible (a reason this SDK does not name reads as not eligible), and `unavailableSentence(notEligible:consequence:)` gives a surface its sentence: its own, unchanged, where the device cannot run Apple Intelligence; *Apple Intelligence is turned off on this device. Turn it on in Settings ▸ Apple Intelligence & Siri to generate summaries here.* (on the Mac, *this Mac* and *System Settings*); or *Apple Intelligence is not ready on this device yet: its model may still be downloading. Try again later.*, each followed by the surface's own last sentence where it had one. The seven sites: both rails' summary sections, both Settings ▸ Summarization panes, a batch run's blocker (`BatchRunBlocker.modelUnavailable` carries the availability, and `BatchRunReadiness.model` replaces `modelAvailable`), the summarizer's error and a collection headnote's Regenerate.
- **The download seam** (`UITestBrowseSeams` 1.5 and 1.6, DEBUG only): `FRUS_UI_TEST_DOWNLOADS=hold|fail` puts a transfer that waits until cancelled, or one that fails as with no connection after 1.5 s, in place of the network, with retries 0.2 s apart and the queue kept in a defaults suite of the seam's own; `FRUS_UI_TEST_QUEUE_DOWNLOADS` queues catalogue volumes at launch; `FRUS_UI_TEST_DOWNLOAD_ON_SIGNAL` starts one on a Darwin signal, for VoiceOver.
- **Two follow-ups the UI runs found.** iOS's Cancel All is text, as each row's own Cancel is, and its question's message names *“Download from GitHub…”* in quotes (`f7a9a6bd`): drawn as a destructive `Label`, the button's title was red and its icon the tint's blue (the first build's screenshot, iPhone 17), and the message, which ended on the button's bare name, *…use Download from GitHub…*, read as cut off in the question's screenshots; it was the app's only long string ending on a bare ellipsis, and the app names a control inside a sentence in curly quotes (*“Send to Zotero Library…”*). And the new suites' own walks (`aec5df5a`), below under **Checked**: Cancel All's question is closed by a tap at its dismiss region's corner, the failure line is found by its words as well as its identifier, and an iPhone scrolls to Download Volume; each test that asks a question or shows the failure keeps a screenshot of it.

**Captures for T2:** `ipad/onboarding-volumes` (HCD-1), whose line gains *to download, about 7 GB once indexed*; the alt text that quotes the old line (the iOS manual's §2.3 figure, the iOS Quick Start, the capture ledger's row 41) is left for T2, as L15 left alt text, since it describes the committed image. `ios/indexing-banner`, taken over Volumes & Storage with Active Downloads showing, is cropped to the banner and the tab bar, so it does not change. No committed frame shows the Mac hub, Free Up Space's note, a failed download or a summary Apple Intelligence cannot make (the simulators run it).

## Session 2026-11-17 — The Collections templates: six named for what they do, planned as L25 (decision 139)

A cloud session read the four templates' recipes (`CollectionPreset`, `FRUSCoreKit/Collections/CollectionExporter.swift`) against the options a collection offers and proposed six in their place, each named for how it presents the documents and which apparatus it carries: *Full text as printed*, *Full text with your annotations*, *Summaries with overview*, *Citations with your notes*, *Citations with archival sources* and *Everything included*. Under the four, Bibliography and the Thematic Index came only with everything on, footnotes were on only in *Scholarly edition*, an Index body never kept the researcher's notes, *Briefing packet* turned on highlights a summary body cannot draw, and the iPhone's chips left *Scholarly edition* out.

The owner took the six ("I like these recommendations. Include a new session in the plan of record to make these changes after L23 and before R5. Do not start implementing from a cloud session."). The plan of record gains decision 139 and row L25, the last row before R5, after L23 and L24 if C1 takes #1915, with its brief: the six recipes, the chips' names, what else moves (the grid, the caption, the test, the manuals, the marketing sublines, the tour draft), the captures for T2, and that it is built on the owner's Mac. ## Session 2026-11-17 — L23: Import from JSON's merge rules in FRUSCoreKit: each record of an export of any format version added, replaced or kept, a newer copy winning in the fields its version carries, with the report a screen shows first (#1915)

**What and why.** Row L23 of the plan of record from 2026-11-15, the first of the two rows checkpoint C1 put into 1.0 on the owner's "In 1.0" (decision 140, written here with L22's merge and #1949's). From `v2` at `ffbd4b77` (#1949, L25's plan, merged after L22's `9e582653`), on `claude/l23-import-json-merge-rules`, in a fresh worktree started by the plan's session. One pull request, "Part of #1915", since the screen is L24's: a code commit (`a7ad17c9`) and a docs commit. Kit code beside the export's envelope with its suites, Foundation only; no app code, no index version, no CloudKit change and no change to the export format.

**Changed.**
- **`FRUSCoreKit/Export/ResearchImportPlan.swift`** (new), public, one API for the app and FRUS Explorer Light:
  - `ResearchImportFile(data:)` reads an export of any format version from 1 to 7 once, through the envelope's tolerant decoder, with FRUS Explorer Light's `frusExplorerLight` key beside it (`WebKey`, each field optional so a later key still reads; one it cannot read is passed over, as the envelope's decoder always has). A file of a later version is refused (`FormatError.newerFormatVersion`), even where it decodes, and one of a version no build wrote (`unknownFormatVersion`).
  - `ResearchLibrarySnapshot` is what a library holds: each record's id and stamp by model type, from an export of the library (`init(_:)`, which reads the stamps as the plan reads the file's) or record by record (`insert(_:id:stamp:)`, `insertSyncedPreferences(createdAt:updatedAt:)`); copies under one id are held at the latest stamp, the copy the app reads, and of several sets of synced preferences the earliest made.
  - `ResearchImportPlan(file:library:)`: for each of the 23 model types, the file's records as items, each added, replaced or kept (`Action`, which has no deletion), a collection's entries and an archive visit's documents and targets as items of their own naming their parent (`parentId`); and the `Report` a screen shows first: per type (`TypeCount`) in the file, added, replaced, kept, set aside and repeated; the file's version and date; the web's key; the fields its version cannot carry (`fieldsNotCarried`); the headnote drafts, summaries without authorship, inert entries and unlinked collections.
  - `ResearchImportRecord`, which every `…Export` record conforms to: its stamp, the record as an import adds it (`resolvedForImport(fromFormatVersion:)`: the app's defaults for what the file's version cannot carry, an older file's readings) and as it writes it over the library's copy (`writtenForImport(over:fromFormatVersion:)`, through `Item.written(over:)`: the fields the version carries from the file, the rest from the copy). - **X2 passed, but only after the iPad's app was force-quit and relaunched. Finding F4:** until then, the iPad's All Notes kept listing *R6 import test*, which had been deleted on the Mac. Read from the code: `AllNotesScreen` renders `NotesPaneSnapshot`, a snapshot of values fetched in its `.task` and again after its own edit sheet closes or a delete (`refresh()`). Nothing observes iCloud's imports, so another device's change shows only when the screen is opened again or the app relaunches. A tap on a stale row finds no note and refreshes (`NotesPaneSnapshot.note(id:in:)` returning `nil`), so it is safe. The Research window and Project Home read live `@Query`s. `build-53`'s copy is identical and no commit since has touched the file, so this is not a regression. It is not a crash, a loss of work or a store check. Placed on the owner's word ("First update"): the first update after 1.0, among the plan's §3 candidates.

## Session 2026-11-19 — R6b: FRUS Explorer on the iPhone Duo simulator, folded, unfolded and half open: no crash, loss of work or store check; one finding, D1, to the first update

**What and why.** Row R6b of the plan of record from 2026-11-15, added during R6 on the owner's word of 2026-11-18 ("add a row to assess the app's behavior on an iphone duo simulator. the assessment should focus on mitigating undesirable behaviors rather than exploiting new opportunities afforded by the device"). The plan's session started it once #1954 had merged, from `v2` at `1f6b51c1`, on `claude/r6b-iphone-duo-f97938`. The aim was defence, not design: find what misbehaves on the Duo, and mitigate before R7 what R6's rule puts there (a crash, a loss of work or a store check). Records only: no file a target compiles changed.

**#1954's merge, recorded** in the plan's R6 bullet, §4 and R6's entry above: `1f6b51c1`, 2026-11-19 06:27:11 UTC, two minutes after it opened, auto-merge off, no issue closed, the tree the head's (`bbc4d03a`).

**How.**
- **The device:** the iPhone Duo simulator `69E4A90C` under iOS 27.2 (24B91016s, on its own runtime), Xcode 27.2. The simulator control's `set_posture` folds it:
  - closed lights the outer screen, 466 × 678 pt;
  - open lights the inner one, 951 × 669 pt;
  - 130° lights the inner one too.
- **The build:** Debug, of `v2` at `1f6b51c1`, built for the Duo under `Scripts/heavy.sh` from this worktree's DerivedData (174 s).
- **The library:** S1's version-75 library (553 volumes, R5's census) cloned into the Duo's container before the app's first launch, with the SwiftData store renamed to the Debug build's `FRUSExplorerDebug.store`. No re-index ran. The first run was checked before, on the empty install.
- **The app-resizability skill**, loaded first. Its prerequisites, read only:
  - the launch storyboard is declared;
  - four orientations are declared for iPad;
  - there is no `UIRequiresFullScreen`.

  All three held. The 14 `userInterfaceIdiom` lines in 10 files were read, then seen on the device. No API the skill modernises showed a fault, so none was changed, as the freeze asks.
- **Driving and evidence:**
  - the simulator control's taps;
  - `simctl io … screenshot --display=1` (outer) and `--display=3` (inner), for each screen;
  - SpringBoard's log, for scene events;
  - the app's log;
  - a copy of T2's remote-control XCUITest, for the accessibility tree (`~/Library/Caches/FRUS-Explorer/r6b/`, never committed).

**What held** (`Planning/iPhone-Duo-Assessment-2026-11-19.md`, nine strips). Each task was begun on the outer screen and taken through an unfold and a fold. Each kept its state:
- the first run's dock, its step and its choice;
- Search's 380 results;
- Filters' staged date limit and Facets' *Years: 2 included*, unapplied;
- the reader's place in the Long Telegram;
- the rail's sheet, twice each way, with no crash;
- a new note's typed line, and then its *Discard Changes?*;
- a collection's subtitle typed in the iPhone's settings drill-in and in the iPad's settings sheet, which the editor swaps at a fold;
- an entry's drill-in, and its Configure sheet, which became the drill-in when folded;
- *Delete "…"?*, which re-anchored to its row (dismissed, nothing deleted);
- Cross-Reference Analytics' chart and Semantic Analytics' map;
- the FRUS Research Guide a queue raises.

## Session 2026-11-20 — Info popovers scroll on the Mac when their text is taller than the room they have: the owner's finding, before 1.0 (1861)'s archive

The owner, before starting R3: "one finding first. info popovers containing more text than can fit in their view need to allow scrolling. example in screenshot." The screenshot was Archival Analytics' About These Figures on the Mac, its text running past the bottom of the screen.

**#1959's merge, recorded** in the plan's bullet for the EditableContent review, §4 and its entry above: `115ff410`, 2026-11-20 17:42:35 UTC, three minutes after it opened (17:39:29 UTC), auto-merge off, no issue closed, a squash onto `8c32d339` whose tree is the head's (`2f2d5f8c`, tree `1fe23700`), read back from GitHub and git.

**The cause.** `FeatureInfoButton` (`FRUSTheme.swift`) scrolled on iOS since #1351, through `ViewThatFits(in: .vertical) { explanation; ScrollView { explanation } }`, the plain stack first so a popover asked for its ideal size hugs it. On the Mac it showed the plain stack ("macOS keeps the plain stack; nothing there has been measured"). A Mac popover asks for its content's ideal height and is never capped, so a long one grew past the screen with nothing to scroll. The cross-reference graph's info popover had no scroll view on either platform.

**The fix.** `InfoPopoverScrolling`, appended to `FRUSTheme.swift`, keeps #1351's construct for iOS. On the Mac it puts the same construct inside `CappedHeightLayout`, which lays its subview out at its ideal height up to `macMaximumHeight` (560 pt, about thirty lines of caption text, below a window's toolbar on the smallest screen the app runs on) and offers it exactly that, so the `ViewThatFits` learns how little room it has and falls through to its scroll view. `FeatureInfoButton` and the graph's info popover use it. Every line of `FRUSTheme.swift` before the appended code stays where it was (the body lost eight lines, its doc comment gained six and the version history two, 1.13), so no EditableContent range moved.

**The tests.** `ResearchRailInfoItemsTests.shortPopoverScrolls` pinned #1351's construct inside `FeatureInfoButton`; it now pins `FeatureInfoButton`'s call of `InfoPopoverScrolling`, the plain content first and exactly one scroll view in the container, and the Mac's `CappedHeightLayout` around it. `cappedLayoutCapsOnlyTallContent` (new) measures the layout through a `UIHostingController`: 120 pt of content keeps its height under a 200 pt cap, and 500 pt is laid out at 200.

**Checks** (Xcode 27.2): `ResearchRailInfoItemsTests`, `EditableContentKeyTests`, `CodingStandardsAuditTests` and `UnconstructedViewAuditTests` on the iPhone 17 under iOS 27.2 (`D6A66A7E`), 98 tests in 4 suites passed; the simulator was shut down after. The Mac check copy, built from the commit (`AppStore` configuration, no new warning) and driven with the owner's grant for it alone: Archival Analytics' About These Figures opened about 550 pt tall, cut at its fourth heading, with a scroll bar; scrolled to the end, its last row, *Collections and classes are different things*, ends in full with the popover's edge below it. Person Analytics' three-row popover hugged its rows, ending under its last sentence with no scroll bar. Chronology's info button is disabled until a range is shown, so it was not used. The copy was quit after. **Not run:** the full unit target, `swift test` (no kit file changed) and the UI suites. The graph's info popover was not opened on either platform. On iOS nothing a reader sees changed in `FeatureInfoButton`, whose construct is the same; the graph's popover gains the same scrolling there.

**Opened as #1960** on the owner's word ("one finding first"), on 2026-11-20, against `v2` at `115ff410`, which had not moved since the fix began. Ready for review, with auto-merge off; no CI check runs on it. Its merge is R3's to record.

## Session 2026-11-23 — FRUS Explorer Light's S29a: WordCloudKit's tokenizers count with a tagger their host gives, and the clouds and references name the tokenizer that counted them

FRUS Explorer Light's row S29a, the first of its phase 4's language rows, one web-authored pull request (FRUS Explorer Light's Mac check 36), from `v2` at `4556c4d5`, on `claude/wordcloudkit-host-tagger`. Linux has no NaturalLanguage, so the web edition will count words with a tagger of its own (its S29c), through this kit's tokenizers and the app's generator, and every count, cloud and reference must say which tagger made it. Nothing the app counts changes.

**The tagger is a protocol, `WordCloudTagger`** (`WordCloudKit/WordCloudTagger.swift`), for what the two tokenizers read of `NLTagger` and nothing else: each word of a text in order with its range and, when the walk asks (`WordCloudTagReading`), its lemma and its lexical class (`WordCloudLexicalClass`: noun, verb, adjective, other), and for the entity lenses each name, joined, with its type (`WordCloudNameType`). A tagger comes with its `NaturalLanguageHealth`, from which the kit already reads a lens's support and a count's word form, and its `WordCloudTokenizerIdentity`, a name and a version.
- **NaturalLanguage's:** `NLTagger` conforms, walking itself with the calls the tokenizers made of it (`wordWalkScheme(of:)`, the string, English, the same options, the class asked at a word's first character, `.joinNames` for names); its health is the gate's verdict for the schemes it was built with. `NaturalLanguageWordCloudTagger` asks the gate for a tagger for each walk with the schemes that walk reads, which are the tokenizers' `wordSchemes` and `schemes` as before. Both tokenizers' `accumulate` without a tagger count with it, so the app counts as it did.
- **A host's:** `accumulate(from:into:tagger:)` on both tokenizers, and `accumulate(from:into:printedInto:tagger:)` on the one pass, count with any tagger on every platform, by the kit's rules. A count of printed forms reads no lemma, whatever a tagger gives. Where NaturalLanguage is missing, `WordCloudMultiLensTokenizer` is no longer unavailable; each declaration that would tag with NaturalLanguage still is, and says why.

**The files name the tokenizer.** `CloudVectorsFile.Provenance` and `KeynessBaselineFile.Configuration` gain `tokenizer`. A stamp that names none was counted by NaturalLanguage at version 1, a fixed identity (`WordCloudTokenizerIdentity.legacyNaturalLanguage`) apart from `naturalLanguage`, whose version moves only with a change to what the app counts; and a stamp of that tokenizer is written without the key. So the four bundled files stand as they are, byte for byte, and while NaturalLanguage's identity is the one they were counted by, `swift run CloudVectorsGenerator` writes the bytes it wrote. `mismatches(against:includeDiplomatic:lexiconsDigest:stopwordsDigest:tokenizer:)` takes the tokenizer that counted the scope, with no default, and refuses another's (`Mismatch.tokenizer`): the web edition's specification's rule, that a reference from another tokenizer is never compared, which no code stated. `BundledKeynessBaseline` passes NaturalLanguage's; the Word Cloud's and Collocates' lists of what keeps a reference from being compared name the new case (`wordcloud.keyness.mismatch.tokenizer`), which the app's own counts never meet.

**The generator takes its tagger from its caller.** `CloudVectorsRunner.run(tagger:cloudLenses:environment:)` counts with the tagger it is given, refuses on that tagger's health, stamps every file with its identity, writes the lenses its caller asks the cloud files to carry (the four by default; any of the six the run counts, each once, `RunError.cloudLenses` otherwise), and reads its overrides from the environment it is given. Each of its passes, the verification walks' included, is bound to the run's tagger. `run()`, which `CloudVectorsGenerator` calls, refuses on this process's verdict and passes NaturalLanguage's. The generator core builds on Linux, with an `autoreleasepool` stand-in where there is no Objective-C runtime.

**Tests:** `WordCloudTaggerTests.swift`, 33 tests in 4 suites, 25 of them on every platform over a stand-in tagger of tables: the single-lens tokenizer's rules, the one pass against the single-lens passes and its printed tally against a printed tokenizer's, which classes a pass reads and when, the identity and the stamps' keys, the bundled files re-encoded, the mismatch; and, on Apple platforms, `NLTagger`'s word and name walks held to the calls the tokenizers made of NaturalLanguage before, the schemes each tokenizer asks for, the mappings and each tagger's health. `CloudVectorsHostedRunTests.swift`, 11 tests in 1 suite, drives whole runs over a stand-in tagger in a folder of its own, which `run()` could never be: the files, their stamps and lenses, the counts against the kit's tokenizer, the refusals, the verification walk finding a tagger whose printed walk differs, and two runs' bytes. `WordCloudKitHostTests` passes the scope's tokenizer to `mismatches`. `WordCloudMultiLensParityTests`, `WordCloudPrintedFormParityTests` and `CloudVectorsGeneratorTests` pass unchanged. Twelve mutations of the change, one at a time, each fail a test.

**Docs:** `CLAUDE.md`'s WordCloudKit entry; `Planning/Generators-Runbook.md`'s CloudVectorsGenerator line; `Docs/EditableContent`, `WordCloudView.swift`'s 27 ranged blocks re-pointed (Amendment-Log).

**Checks**, with Xcode 27.2 on macOS 27.2, clean and unsigned, on an iPhone 17e simulator (iOS 27.0), each heavy job through `Scripts/heavy.sh`, `v2` at `4556c4d5` beside it (the pull request has the figures and the commands):
- **`v2`:** `swift test` 4,567 tests in 537 suites; the unit target 8,183 tests in 990 suites, all passing, 17 tests and 2 suites skipped; both app builds with 2 warning lines each.
- **The branch, at `4626e891`:** `swift test` 4,611 in 542, WordCloudKitTests 123 in 17 (90 in 13 at `v2`) and CloudVectorsGeneratorTests 69 in 5 (58 in 4); the unit target 8,183 in 990, all passing, with `v2`'s skips by name and both builds with its warning lines, line for line; the Mac app's symbols 41 removed and 411 added, each the change's own. The first commit's full run failed the two suites that re-encode a bundled reference, which the second commit's encoding answers.
- **Linux,** in `swift:6.4-noble` over FRUS Explorer Light's `main`, with its package and server patched as its next pin move will patch them, at the first commit (the head's run is in the pull request): built with no warning; every suite passing but the web's parity suite, whose golden files' source digest covers this kit, and which passed whole with the branch's digest in them; WordCloudKitTests 52 tests in 12 suites (30 in 9 at `v2`), the new generator suite 9, with the one named Linux skip; a file of the server's that imports the kits without `@testable` uses every new public name; and each declaration that would tag with NaturalLanguage says why it is unavailable.

**Owed by the owner:** Mac check 36, listed in the pull request, with a word cloud and a Distinctive one drawn in the app; then the merge. FRUS Explorer Light's next pin move (its S26b) carries it.

**Not done:** CloudVectorsGeneratorCore is not shared code by this guide's list, so no boundary test holds it, though FRUS Explorer Light compiles it on Linux from its next pin move; and `CloudVectorsGeneratorTests.swift` tags through NaturalLanguage's gate unguarded in two tests, so on Linux the new suite file compiles alone. Also not done: the UI suites, iOS 26.x, a device and a signed run.

## Session 2026-11-26 — CI: three advisory checks on every pull request, the rules no test checks on Linux, and the build, the package's suites and the unit target on GitHub's Xcode 27 runner

On the owner's word ("Yes, all three"), after the owner asked which CI checks would help. The repository had none: no workflow, no GitHub Actions run ever, and `v2` unprotected, so every pull request merged with no check, and a test ran only when a session ran it on the Mac. GitHub's hosted runners cost nothing for a public repository, and the `xcode-27` image (a preview, actions/runner-images#14404) carries Xcode 27.0 to 27.2 and the iOS 27.0 simulators the suites pin.

**#2016's merge**
- Merged as `b3acd7ad` by the owner on 2026-11-26 at 12:48:45 UTC, a minute after it opened (12:47:35 UTC), auto-merge off. It closed no issue. The merge's tree is the pull request's head (`ff22a67e`, tree `52fda562`), and `v2` stood at `8df01632` while it was open. Its branch is still on `origin`.

**What changed**
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`** (new): three jobs, all advisory, since no branch rule requires them: A and B on every pull request to `v2`, and all three on every push to it, which is after each merge, and by hand. A pull request's new push cancels its run in progress; a push to `v2` lets the run in progress finish, and of the pushes that arrive meanwhile only the newest runs next.
  - **A · hygiene**, on Ubuntu 24.04: `Scripts/check_repo_hygiene.py`.
  - **B · build and package tests**, on `xcode-27` with Xcode 27.2: `swift build --target FRUSCoreKit`; `swift test --no-parallel`, one test at a time, its count of test runs read back; `build-for-testing` of the `FRUSExplorer` scheme for the iPhone 17 under iOS 27.0, which compiles the iOS app, its widgets and both test targets (the scheme builds the Mac app for running, not for testing); the `FRUSExplorerMac` scheme compiled without signing; and a step that fails on any compiler warning but the `GeneratedSummary` and `appintentsmetadataprocessor` residues.
  - **C · unit tests**, on `xcode-27`, but not on a pull request (below): `FRUSExplorerTests` alone on the iPhone 17 under iOS 27.0 but for one test (below), each test allowed 20 minutes, its counts in the job's summary. A failed run also keeps the failures its result bundle records, with their attachments, a crash's report among them, and any crash report the run left on the runner, since a crash of the test host leaves no reason in the console log.
  - **Signing:** a simulator build is signed ad hoc with no team (`CODE_SIGN_STYLE=Manual CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY=- DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=`), which embeds the entitlements without an Apple account, for the keychain suites. The unit-test host never starts CloudKit (`XCTestConfigurationFilePath`), and both script phases run only when archiving, so no build reads anything that lives only on the Mac. Each job keeps its logs as an artifact for 14 days.
- **`Scripts/check_repo_hygiene.py`** (new): six checks that no test makes. The website's pages and the paste kit `--check`; every JSON under `FRUSExplorer/Resources/` parses; each TestFlight note at most 4,000 characters by Python's `len()`; the workflow scripts parse, by Node on CI and JavaScriptCore on a Mac; and no tracked file holds a conflict marker at the start of a line.
- **`CLAUDE.md`**: a paragraph on CI under the lock's habits, which says when each check runs and that nothing waits for them.
- **`FRUSExplorerTests/BackgroundSummarizationTests.swift`**: the empty-scope test waits for the run to end, up to 10 s, where it slept 0.1 s. Its assertion is unchanged.
- **`FRUSExplorerTests/AboutViewTests.swift`**: `InAppBrowserCoordinatorTests` allows its opening page 10 minutes, for WebKit's cold start, and each later wait 120 s, where it allowed every wait 20 s. Its failure names the bound it met, and it prints how long the opening page took. What it asks of WebKit is unchanged.

**C runs after the merge**
- On the owner's word ("Yes move C"), after the owner asked whether B and C run faster on the Mac, for fear that CI's delays would halve a session's pace. Job for job the Mac is about five times faster, by the session log's runs of 16 to 20 November and this pull request's runs 2 to 5: the unit target's tests in 518 to 599 s against 2,351 to 3,058; a clean `build-for-testing` in 153 to 243 s against 12.3 to 20.5 min; `swift test` in 134 s with the package built, or 205 s from empty, against 18 to 22 min from empty, one test at a time; and the Mac app from empty in about 45 s against 4.2 to 5.6 min. B is about 6 or 7 minutes of the Mac's work against 37 to 50, and C 12 or 13 against 60 to 77.
- CI uses no Mac time and never takes the lock, so it slows a session only when someone waits for it, or when Auto-fix wakes a session for a failure only the runner has: each of this pull request's first five runs needed a fix. So C no longer runs on a pull request. It checks `v2` after each merge, and a session's own runs on the Mac stay the check before one; `CLAUDE.md` says not to wait for CI. Without the change to `v2`'s runs above, merges less than C's hour apart would each cancel the C before them, and C would end only once they stopped.

The file was then restored byte for byte, and the changed test drew no warning; one comment line was reworded after the check, to say "about 1 s" where it said "at once".
- **Run 5's change, on the Mac** (iPhone 17, iOS 27.0, one `heavy.sh` call), with one test of `AnnotationReviewTests` made to write to address 0x10. The host crashed each of the three times the test started, and xcodebuild stopped after its second restart. Its console log said only that it was restarting, then `** TEST FAILED **`: it named no crash and no failing test. The result bundle's summary recorded "Exceeded max restart count of 2. (Underlying Error: Crash: FRUS Explorer at …)" and attached the crash report to that failure: 55,909 bytes, `EXC_BAD_ACCESS` at 0x10, the top frame of its faulting thread the test itself. Each crash also left a report in `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports`. The new step's script, run as the runner's shell runs it over that bundle, printed the failure, exported the report and copied the three reports; with no bundle, it said so and passed. The file was then restored byte for byte. The bundle came to 67 MB, and its diagnostics, exported, to 192 MB, which is why the step keeps neither.
- **The steps' failure output**, run under the runner's shell with SIGPIPE ignored, over run 2's log: the old `grep | head` exits 2 before the lines after it, and `grep -m` and `awk` reach them. `check_repo_hygiene.py` passes all six checks with these changes.

CPU-bound suites held every thread of the cooperative pool: unrelated suites all ended near 73 s while `CitationMatchingEngineTests`' sweep ran for 129 s. `swift test --no-parallel` (`237896ec`) fixed it. Measured on the Mac first, no more than 2 of the Zotero suite's tests overlapped with the flag, against 14 without it. That push cancelled C.
- **Run 2, at `237896ec`** (45830765034). A passed in 21 s.   - The session re-read each one's code and recounted it with a script of its own before asking. The skeptics then confirmed all three.

**What it found** (`Planning/Collections-Design-Third-Review-2026-11-26.md`)
- **The count.** 58 findings and the session's A2, merged to 48: 1 at S1, 22 at S2, 25 at S3. None was refuted, seven were re-rated down, and 29 merged errors in the design or the plan were listed.
- **The S1, J1:** *Same settings as…*, built as L47's brief reads, copies the ids that name a document's own headnote and notes. A target then prints the source's, and an edit or a delete through it deletes the source's headnote. INT, ENG and DATA found it independently.
- **The headnote in the collection file** is not yet defined. Off does not travel, a 1.0 app prints a stand-in where the design said it prints nothing, and "with who wrote it" has no key.
- **No row owns the export sheet's sentence.** A *Summaries* export fails on a device without Apple Intelligence even with every summary stored, a 1.0 defect.
- **Selected passages have no home once imported.** The iPad's settings column brings back what Composer v2 removed, with no width rule.
- **Where the volume's heading leads,** headings do not tell documents apart for most volumes before 1952.
- **A tagged PDF needs an API that is newer than the app's 26.0 floor,** or the older `CGPDFContextBeginTag`.
- **Four claims about the volumes were false:** "central files are in", "the only pointers there are" before 1955, the 1952–1954 rule for the volume's own number, and "the volumes before 1952 print no numbers".

**#2022, first: the defect in a test** (decision 183)
- A live 503 cannot be called up, so the online pass moved behind a seam first, with its behaviour unchanged: `ManifestGeneratorRunner.runOnline`, its listing, header fetch and pause handed in, as `SemanticVectorsRunner.run(environment:languageAnalysis:)` takes its inputs. `ManifestFetchFailureTests` drives it over a listing of three of L28's six volumes and a host that answers each from a script, and records the pauses instead of sleeping them.
- **Against the seam before the fix:** seven of its eight tests failed, with 26 issues, and the control (every fetch answered) passed. A 503 every time wrote a manifest of two volumes and returned; a 503 that cleared was not tried again; a 404, a header that does not parse and two failures together each wrote the rest.

**#2022, the fix** (`849b30ba`)
- **The refusal.** A run writes nothing, and leaves the file at `OUTPUT_PATH` as it was, when any volume of the listing has no entry: a fetch, a parse or a listing entry that failed. It refuses too when the entries number fewer than the listing, by whatever road. `RunError.incompleteListing` names each volume and its reason in file-name order, and `run()` prints it and exits 1.
- **Not only a fetch** (decision 183, a few lines in code the row changes): a header that does not parse leaves its volume out by the same road, and L28's step 2 already required `Errors: 0`, which counts it. L28's own description of the fix says "when `Errors` is not 0".
- **The retry.** A fetch that answers a 429 or a 5xx (`TEIHeaderFetcher.isWorthRetrying`) is tried again after 2, 4 and 8 seconds (`retryPauses`), four tries in all, before it counts. Anything else counts at once, a 404, a missing `</teiHeader>` and a transport error among them.
- A failed listing exits 1 as before. The offline overlay is unchanged: it never drops a volume.

**#2023, first: the defect in a test** (decision 183)
- `LayoutStoreTests` drives `run(environment:languageAnalysis:)` over two of the suite's two-kilobyte stores, one under each model with the same width, chunking and prefix. The fixture's layouts name their store and their `layout.bin`, in the form the fixed `build_layout.py` writes, and the refusals' cases were declared and not yet thrown.
- **Against the preflight before the fix:** five of the six tests failed, each "got nil" (the run packed the layout, map and all), and the copy-of-the-store control passed. Driven directly, `pack` packed the 300m's layout over EmbeddingGemma 2's vectors. The other twelve suites passed with the new fixture: 90 tests in 13 suites.

**#2023, the fix** (`7e3e8f28`)
- **The pool names its store.** `pool_docs.py` writes `pool_source.json` last, and removes the last run's first, so a pool that did not finish names none: the store's path (a home folder as `~`), the eight fields of its `run-manifest.json` from `model` to `script_sha256`, and the SHA-256 of `doc_f32_768.npy`.
- **The layout carries it.** `build_layout.py` exits before PCA on a pool without one, or whose matrix is not the one it names, and adds `store` (those fields with the path) and `layoutSHA256` (the SHA-256 of the `layout.bin` it writes) to `layout-meta.json`.
- **The pack checks it.** Handed `STORE`'s run manifest, `SemanticMapPacker.preflight` refuses, before anything is written: a layout whose store differs in the model, its GGUF SHA-256, the width, the chunking or the prefix (`PackError.layoutFromAnotherStore`, naming each field); a `layout.bin` that is not the file its metadata describes (`layoutFileMismatch`, the issue's second road); and a layout that names neither (`unattributedLayout`). The path, the harvest date and the script are not compared, so a copy of the store elsewhere packs, and the corpus stays the document count's to check. `pack` repeats the store check against the vector artifact's own provenance, as it repeats the preflight's other refusals.
- **What a layout written before the fix gets** (the session's to settle): it is refused. It cannot say which store it was laid out over; the scripts remake the shipped layout byte for byte (below); and taking it would leave the stale-`layout.bin` road open, since metadata that names no layout cannot refuse one. The committed `Planning/semantic-map/layout-meta.json` is still 2026-10-15's, so the packer refuses it until the next layout run, R10's step 11, writes the new form. Re-committing it now would only redate the shipped layout.

**What the issues said that did not hold** (decision 183)
- **#2023's document count.** The issue proposed the store's identity as "the model, its GGUF SHA-256 and the document count, from the store's `run-manifest.json`". That file's only count is `totals_this_run`, the last harvest pass's: the 300m's store says 1,142 documents there, the two volumes harvested again on 2026-10-10, where its heads add up to 314,616. So the identity is the model, its weights and the contract, and the count stays the preflight's, from the heads, as it was.

**#2000** (`d927be62`)
- **One rule.** `CollectionExportDocument.includesNotes(options:)` is the rule the web page, the PDF and Word print a document's notes by: its own setting or its section's, which the assembly hands on, else the collection's. The three renderers now call it.
- `citationRecord(options:)` is the document's Zotero item by that rule, its tags kept either way. BibTeX writes through it, and RIS through `ZoteroCollectionExporter.records(for:options:)`.
- **The Zotero send** posts those records, under the options the RIS file is written with (`ExportFormat.zoteroJSON.exportOptions(for:)`). It had posted every item as resolved and read no setting.
- **A shared file** writes a document's notes only where they print and the sheet's switch is on. The section's setting is read through `CollectionOutline.sectionOverrideValues`, the cascade the assembly resolves by. The file's format does not change.
- **The pins** (`CollectionRenderingPinTests`): `everything.bib` and `everything.ris` re-taken (1,061 → 1,529 bytes and 810 → 1,163), since the fixture's notes-off document, `d10`, gained a Zotero item with a note: its record now prints, without the note. With `d10` taken out, a throwaway test (never committed) rendered both to their 2026-10-25 pins, so no byte of the records already pinned moved. **The defect, first** (decision 183)
- `RailAtCompactWidthTests.testUnderReadAResizeAcrossBrowsesTwoPaneWidthKeepsTheRail`, new: under *Open Documents In* ▸ Read it opens the fixture's first document in Browse's two-pane layout by `TwoPaneDocumentTests`' walk, opens its rail, narrows the window to Browse's one-pane stack and widens it again, and requires the rail still open; then a different document must open without it, and the rail is turned on again.
- **On `v2`'s app** (iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), iOS 27.2, Windowed Apps): it failed at the widened window, the rail closed, in 277 s, after every step before it held: the document opened without its rail, the toggle opened it, and the window narrowed under the gate.

- **Two traps of the walk, met on its first two runs:** the volume's Editors' Annotations put its compilation below the fold of a lazy list, so a row must be scrolled to before it is waited for; and in landscape XCUI reports the app's frame in portrait, so `app.swipeUp` landed in the list pane and scrolled nothing. The walk drags in the window's own frame. XCUI's screenshots in landscape are portrait-sized too, so the attachments miss the rail column at the window's right edge; the assertions read the rail's Cite tile.

**The fix**
- **How it differs from the brief's words.** The brief's likely rule compared documents: apply the setting only when a different document opens. A reader built again cannot tell for itself, and comparing with the document the scene last opened would have gone wrong both ways: Read would stop applying when a reader opens again the document it has just left, and the setting would apply to a rebuild after a sheet or another tab had opened another document in between. So the reader tells a rebuild by its moment.
- **`ReaderRebuildLedger`** (`DocumentView.swift`) counts the readers each scene shows, by document. A reader is its document's built again when another reader in the scene still shows the document, or one stopped showing it within a second of this one's start: SwiftUI does not promise the order, and both occur. The per-open task asks first, before anything awaits, since the task waits on the indexing pipeline, which can be busy for minutes.
- **`DocumentView.railSetting(for:isPhone:isBuiltAgain:)`** writes nothing on an iPad reader built again; every open applies the setting as before, a document opened again within the window aside, and an iPhone closes the rail at every start (#404). Research's reader, which Research's own gate rebuilds, keeps its rail too: a probe, run once on the fixed code, passed.
- **A `ReaderRebuild` log line** names each rebuild with the gap it measured. Over the fixed code's run, 64: each 0.00006 to 0.155 s after a reader of its document stopped, or while one still showed it.
- **`BrowserView.swift`:** the two-pane gate's note says that crossing it builds the reader anew, and where the rail is kept.

The plan of record's session started this one for row L41, on `claude/l41-zotero-client-f9a33d`, held until L29 had merged and then begun on the orchestrator's "go" from `v2` at `2db58c5a`, L29's merge. On the merged tree a script applying `EditableContentKeyTests`' rule read all 1,334 ranged blocks, with their 1,363 keys: each key is inside its block's range, and each range this row set starts on its key's line.

**Each defect, first** (decision 183)
- **The control, on `v2`'s client** (`2db58c5a`, the kit untouched), seven new tests written first and run through `Scripts/heavy.sh` with `swift test --filter ZoteroRetryWaitTests`, the package built from empty in 92 s: 20 tests in the suite, the 13 already there passed, and all 7 new ones failed, with 11 issues, each at its defect.
  - **#1924:** a send of one write answered with `Backoff: 5` waited `[5.0]` after its last write, before it returned. Sent again by a new client, the next send waited `[]`.
  - **#1925:** a 429 with `Retry-After: 5` told its caller `Uploading items 1–1…` and waited 5 s, saying nothing of the wait. A `Backoff: 3` on the collection's write was waited under *Creating collection…*, unannounced, before *Uploading items 1–1…*.
  - **#1926:** a `Retry-After` 45 s after the response's `Date` waited `[30, 30, 30]` and threw `rateLimited(30)`; one an hour on did the same over 4 requests, where it should throw at once carrying 3,600; one 45 s after the device's clock, with no `Date`, waited `[30, 30, 30]`.
- Those seven were then made exact for the fix: a `TestClock` the client's sleep moves, so a deadline and a message are compared whole, and a wall clock a test sets for a date counted with no `Date`.

**#1924, the `Backoff`** (`54bf4f86`)
- **Before:** `ZoteroAPIClient.writeRequest` waited a `Backoff`, up to a minute, after Zotero's 2xx and before it returned. So a send's last write, or a send of one write, held the send up to a minute after everything was written, and the next send, by a new client, waited nothing.
- **After:** a 2xx's `Backoff` sets a deadline (`now + min(Backoff, 60)`), and each attempt of each write first waits what is left of it (`holdToBackoff`). A send returns at its last write; the send's next write, or the account's next send, waits the rest.
- **Where the deadline lives:** `ZoteroBackoffDeadlines`, an actor in the client's file, one per process (`.shared`), keyed by the Zotero user ID that every write names in its path. The app makes a new `ZoteroAPIClient()` for each of its three sends, so a deadline kept in a client would be gone at the next send. A deadline that has passed is dropped when read, and a later one is never shortened by an earlier. No API key is kept. `resolveAccount(key:)`, which reads `/keys/` with no user ID, does not consult it.
- **Unchanged:** the 60-second cap, #1916's header rules, and a `Backoff` read on a 2xx alone. A `Backoff` of 0 now holds nothing, where it was a sleep of 0.

**#1925, the waits said** (`54bf4f86`, `8ab12121`)
- **The kit:** before a 429's retry, `retryStatus(seconds:locale:)`, *Zotero is busy: trying again in 30 seconds…*; before a `Backoff`'s wait, `backoffStatus(seconds:locale:)`, *Zotero asked for a pause: continuing in 45 seconds…*. The seconds are whole, rounded up (`wholeSeconds`), and the form is chosen one or many through `CountCopy`, since the count scan refuses a `%lld` before *seconds*. After the wait the step's own message is said again, so the line does not keep the wait while the write runs. A wait of 0 s says nothing.
- **The app:** the collection export sheet already put `status` in its progress line (`preparingMessage`), so it is unchanged. The Mac's Share popover (`DocumentSharePopover`) reads the send's status in the line under its row while it runs, and the iOS Share menu (`DocumentShareMenu`) its send row, with an hourglass, since a menu closes when chosen.

**#1926, a date `Retry-After`** (`54bf4f86`)
- `retryAfterSeconds(_:responseDate:localNow:)`: a `Retry-After` of seconds as before; else an IMF-fixdate (`httpDate(_:)`, a POSIX formatter in GMT, not lenient) counted from the response's own `Date`, or from the device's clock (a seam a test sets) when it has none the client can read. A date before that moment gives no seconds, so the 30 s default; past a minute, `rateLimited` at once with the seconds. `Backoff` stays seconds alone. The two obsolete forms of an HTTP date are not read.

**#1923, the resume: proposed, not built**
- The plan says its design is the owner's. The owner was away overnight, so the orchestrator asked for the proposal in this row's "ready to land" message rather than a question that would hold the session. It is in the group's notes (`L41-1923-resume-proposal.md`), summarised there:
  - **A (recommended):** the kit throws `ZoteroSendStopped` with a progress value (the Zotero collection's key, each written item's key by its URL, the notes written, the batch in flight with its write token), and `send(…, resuming:)` makes no collection and skips what was written; a batch whose answer was lost is re-sent under its own token, and Zotero's 412 for a token it has seen means it landed. The app records the partial send as `zotero-api` with the count written (no CloudKit field) and offers **Finish Sending**, the progress kept in a device-local file for 12 hours.
  - **B:** as A, the progress on the history row, so another device can finish it: new stored properties, joining 1.1's promotion.
  - **C:** record only, and warn before a second send.
  - **D:** ask Zotero what is in the collection, and skip it.
- Zotero's documentation, read for it (2026-11-27): a write token is remembered 12 hours after a successful request and a reused one is refused with 412, carrying no keys; a 200 can carry `successful` and `failed` together; a collection's items list 100 a page with their `url`; there is no lookup by URL.

**A claim of the brief that does not hold** (decision 183)
- The plan has L41 change "how [the collection's send] calls the client" (`CollectionExportSheet.sendToZoteroLibrary()`), and L29 and L41 ordered on it. With the deadline kept per process, the sheet's `ZoteroAPIClient()` holds to it as it is, and the sheet already showed `status`, so `CollectionExportSheet.swift` is unchanged. The order cost nothing.

**Found, and left in §5** (decision 183: offered, not taken)
- Zotero's *Basics* says a 503 during maintenance carries a `Retry-After`; the client reads one on a 429 alone, so a 503 stops a send as *an unexpected error (HTTP 503)*.
- The same page says a `Backoff` can come on any response; the client reads it on a 2xx alone.

**Docs**

## Session 2026-11-27 — L57, the days of Search's date filter: on iPhone and iPad they are read and written in the zone its pickers are in; shown first in New York's zone (30 September for 1 October, 1960 for 1961), a pick found to keep its time of day, and a finding filed as #2033

Row L57 of the plan of record from 2026-11-25 (#2013, decision 187), started by "Development session orchestration" with Wave 2's other rows, on `claude/l57-search-date-filter-zone-d90596`. It read and planned while three rows built, and began on "L57: go", from `v2` at `a7d8e017`. App code and its tests: no package input, so no `swift test`; no stored property and no index version. Commits: `a0240672` (the fix, its tests and the nine re-pointed ranges) and a docs commit.

**#2032's merge**
- L41 merged as `4fa33ba3`, a squash onto `ebacf85a`, at 12:51:53 UTC on 2026-11-27, from its head `7b59ed14`. Its tree, `925c9301`, is the head's. It closed #1924, #1925 and #1926. This entry records it.
- L37's #2031 (`ebacf85a`) is recorded in L41's entry above, and L28's #2026 (`a7d8e017`), where this row began, in L61's.
- This branch took `v2` in at `4fa33ba3` (`f77e1f48`). Three files conflicted, all records: the session log, the Amendment-Log and the plan of record, each resolved with `v2`'s side first and this row's after it. This row's decision, written as 210, is 213, after L33's and L32's, and the plan's status line now names 210 to 212 as well.

**Shown first** (decision 183), at `a7d8e017`, on the iPhone 17 simulator under iOS 27.0, in New York's zone with no zone changed. None of Search's files has changed since `1.0-release`, so this is 1.0's code.
- **The first symptom, in the app.** A UI test handed Search 1 to 31 October 1962 through `AppState.openSearch(_:from:)`, the route Chronology's *Search in this range* takes. Filters' pickers read *Sep 30, 1962* and *Oct 30, 1962*, over the chip *1962-10-01 to 1962-10-31*. In a hosted test the filter held 30 September at 20:00 EDT and 30 October at 19:00 EST, the two midnights in GMT.
- **The third, in a hosted test.** Corpus Analytics' own hand-off of 1961 to 1963 (`AnalyticsSearchHandoff.parameters`), read back as *Visualize in Corpus Analytics* read it (a Gregorian calendar in the device's zone), gave 1960 to 1963.
- **What the issue could not settle: a pick keeps the time of day of the date the picker held.** A temporary `Logger` line in Filters' date section, never committed (its diff is kept at `~/Library/Caches/FRUS-Explorer/l57/probe-job1.diff`), logged From at `1962-09-30T20:00-04:00` before a tap on the 5th and `1962-09-05T20:00-04:00` after; in Tokyo's zone 09:00 stayed 09:00. So the issue's first branch held: west of UTC, after a hand-off or a saved search, a pick was written as the day after the one the picker showed. The UI control, below, then saw it: From at Sep 5 under the chip *1962-09-06 to 1962-10-31*.
- **The same build in Tokyo's zone** (`TZ=Asia/Tokyo`) showed 1 and 31 October, so on this path the defect was west of UTC's, and the UI test's `TZ` reaches the app.
- **Foundation, measured in the same hosted test.** `TimeZone.current`, `.autoupdatingCurrent`, a new `DateFormatter`'s zone and `Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)`'s zone were all New York's, and a `DateFormatter` is strict by default. A strict `yyyy-MM-dd` formatter in a zone reads no date for a day whose midnight a change of clocks skips: from 1861 to 2000, 27 such days in São Paulo, 42 in Havana, 33 in Beirut, 43 in Santiago, 14 each in Tehran and Cairo, 4 in Tokyo and none in New York, each count equal to the days whose first moment is not 00:00. `Calendar.startOfDay(for:)` of the day's noon gave the right day on all of them.

**The fix** (the issue's: the device's zone at every site, not GMT pickers)
- `SearchViewModel.filterDay(of:in:)` and `filterDate(ofDay:in:)` convert at the five sites: a hand-off's and a saved search's read (`applyParameters(_:)`), the facet's year, the search's two days, the *Narrowed by* chip, and the chip's record. The zone is `dateRangeTimeZone`, the device's (`.autoupdatingCurrent`), which only the tests set. *Visualize in Corpus Analytics* reads `dateRangeYears`.
- **Why not GMT pickers:** Filters' pickers are `SearchFilterView`'s, which the Mac's Search window draws over a `SearchViewModel` of its own, so GMT pickers would have moved the Mac's; the app's other pickers and `WordCloudScope.isoFormatter()`'s rule are the device's zone; and a project's range and the filter's first dates are made in it.
- **No one function for both view models.** The Mac converts with a strict `DateFormatter` in the device's zone, which keeps the filter's previous date on a day whose midnight is skipped; `filterDate(ofDay:in:)` takes the day's noon back to its start, so sharing it would have moved what the Mac does on those days. The Mac's file is unchanged.
- **The candidate, `applyProjectDefaults(_:)`:** onboarding makes a project's range in the device's zone (`ManifestStore.corpusYearStart(_:)`), so east of UTC its first day was written a day early. The fix writes it as made; no line of its own.
- **Nothing stored moves.** `SavedSearch` converts its own two dates in GMT both ways and is untouched; no CloudKit field, no index version.
- **The search seam** (`UITestBrowseSeams`, DEBUG only) can carry two days with its words (`FRUS_UI_TEST_SEARCH_ON_SIGNAL_DATES`), for the UI test's hand-off.

**Tests**
- **`SearchDateFilterZoneTests`** (in `SearchViewTests.swift`), 10 tests, every one naming its zone: the two conversions over nine zones from UTC−11 (Pago Pago) to UTC+14 (Kiritimati), with the issue's two tables, São Paulo's skipped midnight and thirteen strings that name no day; and the view model with `dateRangeTimeZone` pinned: a hand-off, a saved search, a chart's years, a pick at four times of day, a facet's year and a project's range.
- **The control:** each site put back in GMT alone, built and run against the suite: the hand-off's read failed 4 tests, the search's two days 6, the facet's year 1, the chip 3, and the years 2.
- `SearchWithinResultsModelTests`' three tests and `IOSFacetNarrowingTests`' one set their dates on days in the device's zone, where they set GMT midnights. `dateRangeFilterIncludedInParameters` is unchanged: it holds anywhere now, and the new suite is the guard. The seam's two days have a test and a wiring check (`BrowseSeamSignalTests`).
- **The row's suites and the files' neighbours** on the iPhone 17 under iOS 27.0 (22 suites, `EditableContentKeyTests` and `CodingStandardsAuditTests` among them): 237 tests, 237 passed.
- **`FilterDateRangeHandOffTests`** (in `MeaningResultsSeamTests.swift`), two tests after a hand-off by the search seam's signal, in New York's zone: the pickers show the handed days, and a day picked in From is the day the chip names. Under iOS 27.0: **iPhone 17, 2 passed; iPad Pro 13-inch (M5), each test alone on a fresh boot, 2 passed.** **The control** (the conversions put back in GMT, iPhone 17): 2 failed, at From's *Sep 30, 1962*, and at From's *Sep 5, 1962* under the chip *1962-09-06 to 1962-10-31*.
  - **On the iPad,** one run of both on one boot ended when `backboardd` aborted in Metal at the second launch, in #1620's frames ("Test crashed with signal kill"); each alone on a fresh boot passed.
  - **On the iPhone,** a run with the app removed met the while-indexing guide over Search at the fresh install's first launch ("Filters did not open"); with the app installed both passed.
  - **Two selectors the first runs taught.** The calendar opens over the sheet's navigation bar on an iPhone, so the test closes it with a tap at From's own place; and that place is fixed on the screen before the calendar opens, since `allElementsBoundByIndex` binds an element to its place among the date pickers and the open calendar takes the first (a coordinate on the bound element picked the 10th). The runbook's entry has both.

**The rest**
- **The manuals** say only that a hand-off carries its range (the iOS manual's *Limit by date*, the Mac's *Date Range*), not what the pickers show, so neither changes. No string changed, so no EditableContent block is added; nine ranges moved and are re-pointed (`Amendment-Log.md`).
- **#2033, filed on the owner's word** ("File it (Recommended)", decision 213): on the Mac's Search and in the word cloud, a day whose midnight a change of clocks skips is read as no date. No row takes it yet.
- **R9's check by hand** stands as the brief wrote it.

**The landing checks,** on the merged tree (`f77e1f48`, tree `11ab5ab3`, with `v2` at `4fa33ba3`), in one `Scripts/heavy.sh` job:
- `build-for-testing` on the iPhone 17: the two known residues and no other warning.
- **The unit target** on the iPhone 17 under iOS 27.0 (`-only-testing FRUSExplorerTests`, the app removed first, the TEI mirror set): 8,370 tests in 1,012 suites passed in 778 s, with the six known issues and 17 skipped.

## Session 2026-11-27 — L30, Citation Lookup: a document number read as the volume prints it, Document 1190b, Document C, Document GT–6, so the app's own citation of 722 documents finds each one, and a number with a letter the volume does not print finds the document of its digits as a best guess

The plan of record's session started this one for row L30, on `claude/l30-citation-printed-number-2e294d` from `v2` at `a17023f9`, L27's merge. The row: #1977, Citation Lookup reading only a citation's digits, so Cite's own citation of a document whose printed number is not whole named another document or none. Commits: `e871df1c` (the failing tests, first), `802b652f` (the fix), `204e915e` (a test the package does not compile), `cbf60d59` (the manuals, EditableContent and the plan) and `89593c96` (the plan's record of the Mac walk), with the landing's.

**#2034's merge**
- L57 merged as `7ccecacb`, a squash onto `4fa33ba3`, at 13:53:31 UTC on 2026-11-27, from its head `68f863d7`. Its tree, `91edcc8f`, is the head's. It closed #2013. This entry records it.
- L41's #2032 (`4fa33ba3`) is recorded in L57's entry above, and so back to this row's start: L37's #2031 in L41's, L32's #2030 in L37's, L29's #2029 in L32's, L33's #2028 in L29's, L61's #2027 in L33's, L28's #2026 in L61's, L31's #2025 in L28's, and L27's #2021 (`a17023f9`), where this row began, in L31's.

**The defect, first** (decision 183)
- **Measured over a full index at version 76** (L31's kept index, 553 volumes): 722 of 314,646 numbered documents print a number that is not whole, as the issue counts them.
  - 82 with a lower-case letter, in 22 volumes, and `frus1955-57v03mSupp`'s `550A`. Each one's digits' document is in its own volume.
  - 628 with a capital prefix, an en dash and a number, in 17 series, all in `frus1958-60v05mSupp`, where no document prints a plain number.
  - 11 single letters, appendices in three 1981–88 volumes.
  - No volume prints two numbers that differ only in case.
- **Four tests committed before the fix** (`e871df1c`), run in the package on `v2`'s code: all four failed, with 61 issues.
  - The app's own citation, made as Copy Citation makes it, in all three formats, marked and plain: `frus1898`'s 1190b and 1190a answered d1190, "Match — document number assigned digitally"; `frus1955-57v03mSupp`'s 550A answered d550 as "Exact match"; `frus1981-88v05`'s appendix C and `frus1958-60v05mSupp`'s GT–6 found nothing.
  - The round trip of every bundled volume by a printed number that is not whole, one of the four kinds in turn: 71 of the 551 volumes not excused missed their own volume in history.state.gov and Chicago form, and 69 in Turabian form, marked or plain, where none did by document 1. The title fragment kept the number's letter, or the whole of "Document C".

**A claim of the brief that does not hold** (decision 183)
- The brief gives the digits fallback as "so that *Document 1190* still reaches 1190b". `frus1898` prints a Document 1190, so that citation asks for 1190 and finds d1190, as the issue's own test expects. The fallback answers only a letter the volume does not print: "Document 1190c" finds d1190.
- The issue's and the plan's `ParsedCitation` is `CitationInput` (`CitationModels.swift:44`).

**The owner's two answers**
- Decision 214: how that fallback's answer is labelled. The owner chose "Best guess (Recommended)": "Best guess — this volume prints no document 1190c", with a note to check the citation, as the engine's rule since #1474 has every result that fails a cited field.
- Whether L30 waits for the by-hand Mac walk, the screen being locked overnight: "Wait for the walk (Recommended)".

**The fix** (`802b652f`, `204e915e`)
- **`CitationInput.documentNumber` is the printed number**, a `String?`, where it was an `Int?` of its digits. `CitationParser.normalizedDocumentNumber(_:)` is the one rule the parse and the Document field read it by: digits lose their leading zeros, a prefix and a single letter are capitals, a prefix's dash is the en dash, and a number's letter keeps its case.
- **The parser** reads a number with one letter, a capital prefix with a dash and digits, and a single capital letter. The title fragment loses the whole number.
  - **The guards are the corpus's own.** Over the 43,496 clauses of the index's text that name the series (from `FRUS` or `Foreign Relations` to the next semicolon, at most 300 characters), a letter read after any capital that followed "document" read eleven, each another kind of document: the pronoun in "this document I have", "Executive Document B" and "S. Ex. Doc. B" of the Senate, "U.N. Doc. A /70". So a single letter is read only after "Document" with its capital or "doc.", not after "Executive", "Ex." or "U.N.", and where a citation ends it. A number's letter followed by a decimal point is the file's: `File No. 851R.00` reads 851, as before.
  - **As written**, two of the 43,496 read a number other than before, an NSC action each (`No. 487a`), which the digits alone misread as documents 487 and 266 too. No clause reads a single letter, and the title fragment of those two alone loses more.
  - The patterns were checked under ICU with the file's own strings, 22 cases.
- **The engine** asks for the printed number, which the index's lookup by number (`document(forDocumentNumber:inVolume:)`, one read of `IndexingPipeline.swift`) now matches as written and then ignoring case: `1190B` finds 1190b, and `550a` finds 550A, not its neighbour 550.
  - A number with a letter that no volume the lookup reads prints falls back to its digits (`letteredNumberFallsBack(_:among:)`), and the document found is a best guess naming the number. Decided once per lookup, "only when the token finds nothing": before 1955 the lookup reads every candidate past a hit, so a fallback volume by volume would have answered a number one volume prints with another's document of its digits as well.
  - No fallback beside a history.state.gov link (#1474 review round 1), in a volume whose index cannot yet say what it holds (#1522), or for a prefix or a single letter.
- **The form.** A paste fills the Document no. field with the printed number, and Structured Entry reads the field by the same rule. On iOS the field's number pad, which typed no letter or dash, is the numbers-and-punctuation keyboard. A link to `…/d373a` fills `373a`, where it filled nothing. Batch reads each note through the parser.
- **Tests:** the four defect-first ones, with exact labels added, and two more in the indexed suite (the once-per-lookup fallback, and none where the index cannot answer); in `CitationParserTests` the three forms, the typed forms, the corpus's own eleven false readings, the title fragment and the field's rule; in `CitationLookupFieldsTests` the Document field. The round trip reads every bundled volume's own citation by each of the four kinds as it reads document 1 (2,212 of 2,212 a format).

**Public API and the symbol diff**
- `CitationInput.documentNumber`, `String?`; `CitationParser.extractDocumentNumber(from:)`, `String?`; new `CitationParser.normalizedDocumentNumber(_:)`, `ConfidenceLabels.numberNotPrinted(_:)` and `.numberNotPrintedNote`. Nothing the indexer stores changes, so no index version.
- `FRUS-API.openapi.yaml`: `/citation-lookup`'s `documentNumber` is a string, with the forms and the fallback; `CitationMatch` is unchanged.
- **The symbol diff** of the Mac debug dylibs (`nm -U -j`, fully demangled, private discriminators and closure numbers dropped), each built unsigned in Debug from empty, `v2` at `a17023f9` from a `git archive`: 253,103 names on `v2` and 253,162 here, 80 removed and 139 added.
  - Removed: `CitationInput.documentNumber` and its initialiser as `Int?`, `extractDocumentNumber(from:) -> Int?`, the engine's `matchByDocumentNumber` and `qualified` with their async parts and closures, and the Parsed Fields section's SwiftUI types.
  - Added: the same as `String?`; the rule, the patterns and their initialisers; the two labels; `letteredNumberFallsBack(_:among:)`; the new `matchByDocumentNumber` and `qualified` with the tuple they return; and the Parsed Fields section's types under the Document field's new modifiers.
  - Nothing of `SearchService` or `IndexingPipeline` moves.

**W2's candidate, offered and left** (decision 183): a pasted citation's result names its document by id alone (`CitationLookupView.swift:779` now). Naming it by its head would take a field on `CitationMatch`, a public type with an OpenAPI schema, or an index read for each row, and the row changes neither. It stays in the plan's §5, which says so.

**The manuals and EditableContent** (`cbf60d59`): both manuals' §11.4 say how a number is read and what the fallback's best guess says, with their *AI Generated* notice kept; `08-Reading-Research-Collections.md` gains the two new strings' blocks, and the twelve ranges the row's lines moved start on their keys again (`Amendment-Log.md`).

**Checks**
- `swift build --target FRUSCoreKit`: no warning. The package's citation suites, 167 tests in 15 suites, passed, the eleven new tests and the three changed among them.
- **The unit target, scoped,** on the iPhone 17 under iOS 27.0: the citation suites, `EditableContentKeyTests`, `CodingStandardsAuditTests`, `CitationLookupViewWiringTests`, `IntegrationTests` and both boundary gates, 257 tests, all passed, with no source warning. Its first run found one test the package does not compile, `CollectionTests`' injected matcher keyed on an `Int` (`204e915e`).
- **The Mac build** (`FRUSExplorerMac`, Debug, unsigned): it succeeded, with the two known residues and no other warning.

  - Copy Citation for `frus1898` d1190b copied "Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, With the Annual Message of the President Transmitted to Congress December 5, 1898 (Washington, D.C.: Government Printing Office, 1901), Document 1190b."
  - Pasted into Citation Lookup, it read Subseries 1898 and Document no. 1190b, and found d1190b, one result, "Match — document number assigned digitally".
  - "FRUS, 1898, Document 1190c" found d1190 as "Best guess — this volume prints no document 1190c", with its note and the digital-number label after it.

- **Today 5,536 open nothing; with the row's rule, 559.** In a volume's Contents, 2,306 of 19,453 did and 89 do. All 2,472 to a roman page did (1,493 in a Contents, 64 into another volume), and 89 do. Of the 3,056 to an arabic page no document holds, 2,594 open a division. Of the 4,202 links that now open a division, roman or arabic, by its subtype: `index` 1,047 (the Index, and the lists of abbreviations and of persons, which the corpus types alike), a referral 734, a compilation's title page 718, a chapter's 515, a preface or an introduction (`preface`) 384, the Sources 249; 775 more open the section a roman page is printed in.

**The fix** (`c92b89b3`)
- **The grammar** (`FRUSURLScheme.resolveCrossRefTarget`): `CrossRefDestination.romanPage(volumeId:page:)`, for `pg`/`page`, an optional `_`, and letters `PageNumber.parse(_:)` reads as a roman numeral (`FRUSURLScheme.romanPage(ofAnchor:)`); any other page anchor stays `.unresolved`. Nothing the index stores moves: `SettledCrossReferenceTarget` keeps such a row as collected, as it kept `.unresolved`; both page passes filter `GLOB 'pg_[0-9]*'`; the converter's citing hint, `PageReferenceForm` and the generators read `.page` alone. CrossRefKit's twin has the case (`RefDestination.romanPage`, `CrossRefGrammar.romanPage(ofAnchor:)`), `CrossRefGrammarAppParityTests` holds the two to each other over eight cases, and `citedDocument` is nil for it, so neither the edge nor the flow generator's output moves.

**The rule, the kit's** (`FRUSCoreKit/CrossReference/CrossReferenceGraphDisplay.swift`, display 1.3)
- `CrossReferenceGraphDisplay.capture(nodes:edges:graph:dateValues:dateWindow:)` → `CrossReferenceGraphCapture`.
  - It reads the graph as built (the view model's `baseDisplayNodes`), never the timeline's displayed nodes, whose date clusters fold documents.
  - It takes every document at the depth loaded, in the display build's order, nearest first. A volume cluster's documents come from the loaded graph's own direct references, in the cluster's place by key; a date cluster gives its members; documents in volumes not downloaded are taken too.
  - Page nodes are left out and counted. The archival nodes are reported by the saved documents they hang off, by the edge that ties them.
- **A brushed range.** The view model passes `drawnDateWindow`, the brush while the timeline is drawn and `nil` in the network.
  - A document dated outside the range is left out, and an undated one stays, as the Undated column draws it.
  - A closed volume cluster's documents are held to the range by their own dates, so the set is the same whichever clusters are open.
- **Words:** the central document's label (`frus1952-54v02p1, Doc. 16`, the graph's own `graph.node.docNumber %@`), the depth, the range's two days, the name and description, the cited-pages line, the empty case, the picker's line and the toast.
- **Tests:** `CrossReferenceGraphCaptureTests`, 16, in the file of the graph's suites, compiled in Xcode and in the package.

**Save as Working Corpus** (`f7cf1b7d`)

- **Notes that do not print** (`FootnotePrinting`): no popover, no entry in the notes, and the call the volume's number as text, or nothing for a note it printed unnumbered (#2007).
- **One heading rule** (J32): the collection's title is level 1, a section of level *L* is *L* + 1, a document one below its section, the volume's heading under a title one below that, an attachment's one below the volume's, and the notes' one below the document's. Past six the web page writes a paragraph with the heading role and `aria-level`; Word writes each level as its outline level.
- **No placeholder in an export** (J10): only the live preview tells its author a requested headnote has nothing stored.
- **The contents rows** (`CollectionContentsRow`): the documents alone numbered, alike in the three (#1993); a *Header & Dateline* row the heading's words and the dateline (#1994, #2002); a titled row with *As published:* and the volume's heading under it, and in *Citation* style the citation after (J46).
- **Each line its own run with its role** (J19): the PDF's ranges carry `PDFCollectionExporter.planRoleKey`, for L60.

**Each format**
- **Web page:** the contents an `<ol role="list">` writing its own numbers; the headings at their levels; the calls of notes that do not print as text.
- **PDF:** the contents list runs on over as many pages as it needs (#1984); the source note follows the text and prints whole; a research note flows under its document; a summary prints under its label, where 1.0's PDF alone printed none (found in the review pass).
- **Word:** the contents list is the plan's rows, each linked to a bookmark at its entry, with no page field and no tab leader (the run above), where it was one `TOC` field; each note is marked with the volume's number, at its call and its note (#2001); the section styles are one outline level down (J32); the lines above the text keep with it (J16).
- **The outline** (J38): an entry's row in the collection editor and the Mac's manager reads the title with the volume's heading under it.
- **#2005's sentence:** a generated headnote names the app's model among the sources. The statement as §3.7 redesigns it stays L58's.

**R2b's finding, taken on the owner's word** ("Take it into L34", decision 217)
- Where a collection names no summary prompt, an entry's headnote card, and the headnote the export printed, took the first summary the store returned, the oldest, where the document's rail shows the newest. A document at summary depth took its prompt's oldest the same way.
- `SummaryRecency` (`FRUSCoreKit/Models/SummaryRecency.swift`) is the rail's rule over values, by when each summary was made, then saved, then its id; `GeneratedSummary.ranksAbove(_:_:)` reads its records through it. The assembly's headnote, the inspector's card and the resolver's summary under a prompt take the newest by it.
